newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: LITHUANIA LEADER WORRIED BY WAR CRIME CASE DELAY.
newsitem.headline: LITHUANIA LEADER WORRIED BY WAR CRIME CASE DELAY.

text.p: Lithuanian President Algirdas Brazauskas, currently hosting Hungarian president Arpad Goncz, said on Wednesday delays in prosecuting an alleged Lithuanian war criminals were overshadowing the country's relations with Jewish organisations.

Brazauskas last week received a letter signed by 92 of the 120 Israeli Knesset members asking the president to put pressure on the authorities to prosecute alleged Lithuanian war criminals, including the most notorious, Aleksandras Lileikis.

"I am going to question the prosecutors office about the course of the case (against Lileikis)...It seems to be delayed," Brazauskas told a joint news conference with Goncz, who is in Lithuania on an official visit.
"Our relations with the world Jewish community have been clouded by this issue," Brazauskas added.
Lileikis returned to Lithuania last June after a U.S. federal court revoked his U.S. citizenship on the grounds he concealed war-time activities when he entered the United States.

U.S. prosecutors and Nazi hunters allege that Lileikis handed scores of Jews over to death squads when he headed the Vilnius branch of the Lithuanian security police during the Nazi occupation of the Baltic state.
"We strive to ensure that all of the legal measures are carried out...50 years is a long time but justice must prevail," Brazauskas said.
The letter from the Knesset members was organised by the Simon Wiesenthal Centre in Jerusalem.
It called on Brazauskas to honour a promise he made to the Knesset two years ago when he vowed the Baltic state would take action against alleged war criminals.
Lithuania has been accused of dragging its feet in the case of Lileikis and other Lithuanians suspected of playing a role in the Holocaust.
Historians say some 94 percent of the country's pre-war Jewish population of 220,000 was murdered during World War Two. 051430 GMT mar 97
